name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add one high-contrast skip link at the very top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. This fixes the biggest keyboard navigation pain point—users who rely on assistive tech can skip repetitive headers and nav blocks instantly. The trade-off is a single extra element at the top of each page, which is negligible compared to the universal accessibility gain.

name: Reader
text: A single high-contrast skip link fails users who rely on screen readers when the page reloads or dynamically updates—focus never reaches `<main>`, trapping them in a loop. Instead, pair it with `role="main"` *and* a visible skip link that persists after dynamic content changes; test with VoiceOver and NVDA to confirm focus shifts correctly. Settle it by running a 5-minute screen-reader test on a live page with dynamic updates.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a skip link that jumps to `<main role="main">` and keep it visible at all times. This guarantees screen reader users land where the page’s main content begins, even after dynamic updates. The trade-off is one extra element in the DOM, but it fixes the trap without extra scripting.

name: Reader
text: Reader: A visible skip link *and* `<main role="main">` still fails when dynamic content loads—VoiceOver users get stuck if the new content isn’t wrapped in `<main>` or if the skip link’s target ID shifts. The real risk is assuming static markup covers dynamic cases. Test with a page that loads fresh content via AJAX and confirm focus reaches the new main content without manual intervention.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Add a **persistent, high-contrast skip link** that always jumps to `<main role="main">`—tested with VoiceOver on dynamic pages—owned by Ramp.
